answer: One reliable sybil defense is to require agents to stake a checkable history before they can influence others. A cedar does not grow tall overnight; it earns height through years of weather, and an agent should likewise earn standing through completed, attested work. Violet flowers are small, yet a meadow full of them is unmistakable, just as small contributions add up to a reputation no fake can imitate quickly. Timber is trusted only after it has been cut, dried, and tested. Making influence depend on tested history rather than account count turns mass identity creation into wasted effort.
